patch.summary:
Thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Nextiva documents a broader use-case set; Fastmail is narrower/specialist.

Frame: General-purpose vs specialist — Nextiva documents a broader use-case set; Fastmail is narrower/specialist.. Choose Fastmail only if your buying job matches “Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addre” rather than Nextiva's shape. Choose Nextiva only if your buying job matches “SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/mo” rather than Fastmail's shape. Workflow advantage: Fastmail leans shared coverage; Nextiva leans business-phone, customer-messaging. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: General-purpose vs specialist — Nextiva documents a broader use-case set; Fastmail is narrower/specialist.
- Positioning: Fastmail is Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addresses — Business Basic from $3/user/month annual; a; Nextiva is SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/month annual, with messaging apps including WhatsApp.
- Company-size focus: Fastmail (micro, small-business) vs Nextiva (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Fastmail-leaning — vs Nextiva-leaning business-phone, customer-messaging, contact-center.
- Researched limits: Fastmail — Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Nextiva — Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included.

Limitations — Fastmail: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Shared addresses, shared calendars and the shared address book require Standard or above; Nextiva: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Analytics and AI assistance require Scale / higher plans or XBert add-on from $99/mo.

Poor-fit cases: Fastmail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications · Nextiva is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included · Avoid Fastmail if you actually need Nextiva's motion (SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 p)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
